newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Unit linked behind Skandia's 9-mo profit hike.
newsitem.headline: Unit linked behind Skandia's 9-mo profit hike.

text.p: Swedish insurer Skandia reported on Friday a modest increase in profits for the first nine months of the year, bolstered by a 52 percent leap in volumes for the group's unit linked business.
Operating profit for the period came in at 2.77 billion crowns ($418.6 million), a six percent rise on the 2.62 billion crowns posted for the corresponding period last year.
The result was shored up by a 48 percent jump in earnings from unit linked assurance to 1.06 billion crowns. Premiums in this business rose 52 percent to 22.71 billion crowns.

"We've had excellent growth in Unit Linked, almost all of which was made in the United States and Britain. We had good growth in Sweden, too, but the market is of course much smaller," Skandia spokesman Anders Lundblad told Reuters.

Premiums in the non-life reinsurance and insurance business fell to 17.32 billion crowns from 18.63 billion in what Skandia said was the result of a stronger Swedish crown in translating premiums from international operations.
"Currency variations have had a negative impact on the group's premium income, by 10 percent, compared with the corresponding period in 1995," it said.
The technical result from the non-life insurance and reinsurance business was sharply down on the same period last year, mainly due to higher claims costs in the first six months of the year.

Investment income -- which consists of direct investment income and changes in the value of investment assets -- showed good growth 1.99 billion from 1.40 billion in the first nine months of last year.

This, Skandia said, was mainly thanks to "very strong growth in share portfolios," as well as positive cash flow from operations and cash generated on sale of assets, which boosted return on investments.
The group's Swedish niche bank SkandiaBanken reported earnings of 59 million crowns, down from 62 million in the first nine months of 1995.
The group's net asset value at September 30 climbed to 18.14 billion crowns, or 177 crowns per share, from 16.25 billion at the turn of the year.
Anders Lundblad said the relatively small increase in operating profits compared with last year was a result of the strength of Skandia's 1995 performance.
Although he declined to comment on the group's outlook, Lundblad told Reuters the group had fared well so far in the fourth quarter.

"What we've seen is that things have gone better in the third quarter of this year compared with the first two. I think this trend will continue, and so far this quarter things look good," he said. ($=6.6160 Swedish crown) ($ = 6.616 Swedish Crowns)
